overall_summary: The channel's growth is heavily driven by extreme exoplanet mysteries and sensory-focused space facts, which consistently outperform other niches. In contrast, generic psychology and brain-related facts are highly saturated and fail to gain traction, showing extremely low view counts.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,055 views), 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (976 views), and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies' (623 views) represent the channel's top-performing tier.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on bizarre exoplanet conditions, utilizing highly visual and paradoxical hooks that challenge common understanding of physics.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What Does Outer Space Actually Smell Like? (Steak/Space)' (368 views) and 'The Largest Ocean in Space' (460 views) show strong performance by linking abstract cosmic concepts to familiar sensory experiences.
winning_patterns.action: Frame complex astronomical phenomena using everyday sensory analogies (smell, taste, touch) to lower the cognitive barrier and increase curiosity.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) consistently fail to capture audience interest.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from standard psychology facts unless they can be framed with a highly dramatic, cinematic micro-story or a shocking visual hook.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Sharks Are Older Than WHAT?!' (8 views) drastically underperformed 'Sharks Are Older Than Trees?' (302 views), and 'Your Head Is Aging Faster Than Your Feet!' (52 views) underperformed 'Why Your Head Is Older Than Your Feet' (262 views).
weak_patterns.action: Avoid clickbait questions that hide too much context, and prefer 'Why' hooks over declarative statements to establish a clear curiosity gap.

next_video.concept: The giant planet made of pink cotton candy that shouldn't exist (WASP-193b).
next_video.opening_direction: Start with a close-up visual of fluffy pink cotton candy spinning in a machine, then zoom out to reveal it's a massive planet floating in deep space.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that despite being 50% larger than Jupiter, this cosmic giant is so light and airy that it has the exact density of cotton candy, defying standard planetary physics.
next_video.reason: Leverages the highly successful exoplanet mystery formula, utilizes a strong sensory hook (cotton candy), and maintains the optimal 16-second duration of our top-performing videos.

experiment: Test a cinematic historical storytelling Short focusing on a bizarre ancient mystery (e.g., the Antikythera mechanism or a strange historical event) using a story-first approach to see if it can match the high baseline of the space mystery videos.
